items.title: The director of Donnie Darko on why the film is so misunderstood
items.description:

items.title: Francis Fukuyama on why we’re better than our ancestors
items.description:
In 1675, Madame de Sévigné wrote a letter to her daughter about a musician “broken on the wheel.” This meant being strapped to an X-shaped cross, where an executioner would systematically break the victim’s bones, leaving him to die slowly from blood loss or dehydration. items.title: Google CTO: A unifying theory of life, intelligence, and technology
items.description:
From von Neumann’s blueprint, which predated the discovery of DNA, to viral genes that now help form our memories and placentas, Blaise Agüera y Arcas argues that function defines life more than material does, and that AI belongs in the same story. He explains why he thinks AGI is already here, and gives a blueprint for using AI without sacrificing your own mind. 
 This video  Google CTO: A unifying theory of life, intelligence, and technology  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: The Second Amendment has a hidden origin story
items.description:
Malcolm Gladwell argues that almost everything most people believe about the Second Amendment is wrong. Guns weren’t widely owned in 18th-century America. The militias didn’t win the Revolutionary War. And the amendment that guaranteed their survival was written to protect one thing in particular: the armed slave patrols that Southern plantation owners depended on.

items.title: Ask Ethan: Do evaporating black holes ever lose their event horizons?
items.description:
Here in our Universe, there are few objects more awe-inspiring or mysterious than black holes. First theorized to exist back in the late 18th century, they represent a region of space where so much mass and energy is confined within such a small volume that, from within it, nothing can escape: not even light itself.
